recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-9107 unless a separate work-group decision requests changes to the current ImplementationGuide.definition.page.generation element or value set.
issue_request: FHIR-9107 asked that ImplementationGuide.page.kind not have GuidePageKind as a required value set because the values were incomplete and too tailored to FHIR publication tooling; it suggested making the value set extensible. Jira is Published with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification and resolution text saying the request was overtaken by other changes to ImplementationGuide.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-9107. Source history shows the relevant application happened indirectly: b319b6a0dac9ca63360026abf48be963f7b143b9 reworked ImplementationGuide and removed the old ImplementationGuide.page.kind element from the active page structure, and 75410cdf57738f0d8d70655324aee865801f6aaf added ImplementationGuide.definition.page.generation with a separate GuidePageGeneration binding.
additional_context: ImplementationGuide is active in source/fhir.ini. The current structure definition has ImplementationGuide.definition.page.source[x], name, title, generation, and nested page children, but no ImplementationGuide.page.kind. The remaining required page binding is GuidePageGeneration, whose code system contains html, markdown, xml, and generated; this is a narrower generation-mode signal, not the broad GuidePageKind taxonomy from the issue. FHIR-I minutes from 2018-07-09 corroborate the Not Persuasive with Modification disposition, and a March 2018 Zulip thread shows the R3 page kind model was being converted toward generated-page behavior.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. Weakening the current required GuidePageGeneration binding would change a different current element and is not supported by FHIR-9107; the original required GuidePageKind binding is already absent from the current active source.
